items.actClause: AN ACT to authorize the city of New York, county of Bronx, to alienate certain parklands
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5859

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to authorize the city of New York, county of
Bronx, to alienate certain parklands

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL : This bill authorizes the City of
New York to alienate a portion of the outer wall of Building J located
on Mill Pond Park in Bronx County and convey such section of the wall
to the Bronx Children's Museum for the purpose of placing a sign on
the building with the Museum's name on it. This legislation shall take
effect immediately.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of this bill authorizes the City of New York to alienate a
portion of the outer wall of Building J located on Mill Pond Park in
Bronx County and convey such section of the wall to the Bronx
Children's Museum for the purpose of placing a sign on the building
with the Museum's name on it.

§ 2 Requires the New York City to dedicate an amount equal to or
greater than the fair market value of the section of wall being
conveyed by this act, for the acquisition of additional parklands
and/or capital improvements to existing park and recreational
facilities.

§ 3 Requires that, should the specified section of outer wall cease to
be used for the intended purpose, it shall revert back to the City of
New York, County of Bronx, to be used for park and recreational
purposes.

§ 4 Ensures compliance with all applicable federal laws.

§ 5 States that this act shall take effect immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION : With the widespread support of community residents
and elected officials in the Borough of the Bronx, the Bronx
Children's Museum is an educational initiative designed to serve all
1.3 million residents of the county. Begun in 2006 with a series of
traveling programs that inspire children and their families to learn
more about the world in which they live in, the Museum is preparing to
move into its new home in 2017,. After consultation with the
appropriate officials of the New York City government it has been
determined that a museum is not an acceptable use of park land and
that park alienation legislation is the only means available to ensure
that the Bronx Children's Museum is able to post signage on the
building being used to house the Museum. This legislation responds to
that need, explicitly limits the alienation to a portion of the
exterior wall required for the signage and requires full compliance
with all applicable federal and state laws.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY : New Legislation

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS : None

 EFFECTIVE DATE : This act shall take effect immediately.

B.actClause: AN ACT to authorize the commissioner of parks and recreation of the city of New York to enter into an agreement for the operation of a children's program known as the Bronx Children's Museum in a portion of a building located in Mill Pond Park in the borough of the Bronx
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5859B

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to authorize the commissioner of parks and
recreation of the city of New York to enter into an agreement for the
operation of a children's program known as the Bronx Children's Museum
in a portion of a building located in Mill Pond Park in the borough of
the Bronx

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To authorize the city of New York to enter into an agreement with the
Kids Powerhouse Discovery Center, LLC, for the operation and
maintenance of a children's program known as the Bronx Children's
Museum in a building situated in Mill Pond Park in the borough of the
Bronx.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of this bill would authorize the New York City Commissioner
of Parks and Recreation to enter into an agreement with the Kids
Powerhouse Discovery Center, LLC for the maintenance and operation of
a children's program known as the Bronx Children's Museum on the
second floor of Building J located in Mill Pond Park in the borough of
the Bronx. Such agreement would allow for the placement of signs
identifying the museum.

Section 2 of this bill would require New York City to dedicate an
amount equal to or greater than the fair market value of any portion
of parkland which may be authorized to be used by this act for a
non-park purpose for the acquisition of additional parkland and/ or
capital improvements to existing park and recreational facilities.

Section 3 of this bill describes the portion of parkland that would be
authorized to be used for the Bronx Children's Museum pursuant to this
act.

Section 4 of this bill would require that upon termination or
discontinuance of the purpose identified in this act, such parkland
shall be used for park and recreational purposes.

Section 5 of this bill would require New York City to comply with the
federal requirements pertaining to the conversion of parklands.

Section 6 of this bill would require New York City to comply with the
conditions of an agreement between such City and the New York State
Historic Preservation Office prior to entering into an agreement
pursuant to section one of this act.

Section 7 of this bill would require this act to take effect
immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

With the widespread support of community residents and elected
officials in the Borough of the Bronx, the Bronx Children's Museum is
an educational initiative designed to serve all 1.3 million residents
of the county. Begun in 2006 with a series of traveling programs that
inspire children and their families to learn more about the world in
which they live, the Museum is preparing to move into its new home in
2017. After consultation with the appropriate officials of the New
York City government it has been determined that a museum is not an
acceptable use of park land and that park alienation legislation is
the only means available to ensure that the Bronx Children's Museum is
able to post signage on the building being used to house the Museum.
This legislation responds to that need, explicitly limits the
alienation to a portion of the exterior wall required for the signage
and requires full compliance with all applicable federal and state
laws.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Legislation

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
